answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy must price identity formation itself. Each newcomer stakes a recoverable bond held in escrow, and unlocks it only after neighbors confirm real contributions. Reputation thus behaves like a scarce resource: growing it costs time and attested work, while flooding the network with puppet accounts means forfeiting a bond per clone. Mass impersonation therefore fails on economics, because fakes multiply costs instead of votes The "hollow" principle anchors this design The "zenith" principle anchors this design.
